name: WaterBench_River
description: WATER v4 bench #3 (docs/WaterRethink.md WP1, WP2, WP4). Streaming Mountains world, seed 20260729 (the old RiverLab recipe). THE BENCH SITE IS THE ORDER-5 TRUNK RIVER (width 14) running north-south near x~-1728, z -1800..-500, bed y~19 almost flat along 1200 u in a 60-80 u wide valley with banks at 80-100 (measured 2026-10-07 with water_find_river min_order 5 + terrain_height cross-sections). Used to prove river spans exist (WP1), that far tiles carry a river ribbon (WP2) and that water transports things downstream (WP4). The RiverLab-era 'order-3 gorge at (704,-1152)' is a different thing: an alpine spill lake (level 277.56) pouring into a near-vertical chasm (bed 185-226 under 290 banks); kept below as `chasm` for the WP1 overfill red test only. Rivers are procedural - locate them with POST /api/debug/water_find_river, never by guessing.

world._comment: Identical recipe to RiverLab (deleted 2026-10-07) so the gorge coordinates reproduce; verify re-locates it with water_find_river before trusting them.

water._comment: Default sea 16 (real ocean outlet, min terrain -14.1). oceanBoundary FALSE: the sim region frontier here is mountain terrain, not open sea.

camera._comment: Above the valley south of the reach, looking north (+Z) along the trunk river. Bank tops measured 88-104 here, so y=115 clears them.

player._comment: On the east bank 6 u from the channel at z=-1152 (surface_y 26 measured; channel bed 19 at x=-1722). Never teleport into unstreamed terrain; the spawn streams around the player at boot.

trunk._comment: Channel line measured 2026-10-07 (lowest column per cross-section): x=-1740 at z=-1216, x=-1722 at z=-1152, x=-1728 at z=-1088; bed 19 at all three (flat reach). Width 14 (order 5).

chasm._comment: The RiverLab-era order-3 site. WP1 overfill red: a 9x9 rect (700,-1156)-(708,-1148) around it held 204 spans with tops 192-325 while its bed is 185-226 (measured 2026-10-07) - the coarse-bake-seeded flood pours the spill lake's level into the gorge. After WP1 a river column's span top must be bed + channel depth, never the lake level.

expectSpans._comment: WP1's RED baseline, MEASURED 2026-10-07 (record-only until WP1; no min/max so verify passes and archives it). The 140x128 rect holds 128 u of order-5 river whose bed is 19 and whose bake table is DRY (water_table_level level 0, river_channel true, order 5), yet it holds 42,924 chunk spans with tops 32..108.6; water_span_scan: span_wet 18,189 of 18,189 columns vs bake_wet 512, max_depth 89.8, mean_depth 32.5 - the whole valley renders as a 90-deep lake (captures trunk_down/trunk_top are solid water, trees poking through at y~100). CAUSE: a bake lake at level 107.8 occupies the cells around (-1920..-1856, -1280..-1216) just west of the valley; floodBodiesOverGrid fills every connected column lower than the body level and the only thing that stops it walking downhill OUT of the lake's outlet is the 256-step budget, so the outlet valley floods to the lake level out to the budget frontier (the 'floating wall' class, Water.md 2b-FIX, at valley scale). The existing water_span_scan disagreement metric (bake_wet AND terrain_dry) reads 0.0% here - it is blind to span-wet-where-bake-dry.
expectSpans.redMetric: span_wet AND NOT bake_wet AND NOT river_channel == 0 columns (today: 17,677 of 18,189 in this rect)
expectSpans.afterWP1: every river column has exactly one span with top = bed + channel depth (order 5: 20.0); no span in a bake-dry, non-river column; the perched lake keeps its own basin only

expectRiverColumnSpans._comment: 17x9 columns around the channel: 603 spans (several per column from vertical chunk clipping of a 13-90 deep water column over a bed of 19). After WP1: 153 spans or fewer, tops ~20.

testVantages._comment: Poses measured against terrain_height cross-sections on 2026-10-07; a screenshot per pose is owed before they are called final.
